pr_title: Default collection install to first path in COLLECTIONS_PATHS
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Provide a sane default install path value for `ansible-galaxy collection install`

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
`ansible-galaxy`

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Fixes #62869
pr_comments:
cc @acozine @gundalow
[click here for bot help](https://github.com/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/master/ISSUE_HELP.md)
<!--- boilerplate: notify --->

Sounds correct to me. And in line with the original intentional for 'ansible-galaxy collection install'.

The default for `C.COLLECTIONS_PATH` is `~/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections` 
(https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/config/base.yml#L221) so the docs and behavior sound correct.

The only case that comes to mind that might be odd is if `~/.ansible` doesn't exist, but there are tons of other default config values that use ~/.ansible as well, so not a unique problem for collections_path.

Testing this out, it seems to do the right thing with a default config (or an ansible.cfg that doesn't provide `collections_path`).

`ansible-galaxy collection install alikins.collection_ntp` installs to ~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/alikins/collection_ntp as expected.

I’m going on leave now so I can’t really do much, the original decision was to not have a default because we couldn’t agree on what it should be. This needs to have a wider discussion before it is merged

I agree that having the default be used would match current end user usage / expectations coming from the world of role installation.

`~/.ansible/collections` has my vote, if the idea is we're moving to a more user-centric view of Ansible content (vs. what I remember being the old default, of `/etc/ansible/*`).

We absolutely need to have a default path. I don't think we can expect people to know the correct directory to install collections to, especially if we want to convince people that collections don't significantly increase the complexity of managing your ansible installations. If we don't specify a default I'm going to have to be forced to append `-p ~/.ansible/collections` to the install command on galaxy when we go to updated it from `mazer`, which is possibly the worst way to do a default path for this.

Changes requested by @bcoca go beyond the scope of this PR, as it would require taking apart logic in the role install [found here]( https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/galaxy/role.py#L294) and logic in the collection install [found here](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py#L160). I'm not willing to tinker with all of that and take on the risk of breaking things.

Also, it's been suggested that C.COLLECTIONS_PATHS might not contain a value. I've tested this and found it to not be possible. If you don't define an env var, and you set `collections_paths` in ansible.cfg to "", it defaults to your home directory. The only problem that would arise then is a user that doesn't have a home dir, and in such a case I would expect Ansible to detect this during the process of constructing the configuration and either raise an exception or choose some other value.

issue_context.title: Missing default collection install path
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
`ansible-galaxy collection install` currently requires the user to specify an install path using the `-p` option. Galaxy currently generates and displays the CLI command for installing a collection. There is no way for Galaxy to determine a value for `-p`, and hard coding a default value into Galaxy makes no sense.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
`ansible-galaxy`

##### ANSIBLE VERSION

FWIW, this is expected as we decided to not default the path and require users to explicitly provide it on the CLI. See https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/60216

I'm not sure the associated PR is the way we want to go should we decide to not make it mandatory, and will require broader discussion.

review_comments:
The only odd behavior I can create is if I set 'collections_paths = :'  (an empty list)

``` ini
[defaults]
collections_paths = :
```

In that case, the collection ends up getting installed into $PWD/ansible_collections/.
But I suspect that is a general issue with config types of 'pathspec' and not specific
to collection_path.
Yeah, this should probably be an error if the config has explicitly removed the paths...
